builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: MAEP replaces modality-agnostic expert-pruning importance metrics with a training-free, single-forward-pass metric that separates vision-side pruning signals from text-side preservation signals for MoE-based MLLMs. Cost is limited to a calibration forward pass and permanent removal of experts, with no retraining; inference speed is largely unchanged since it removes parameters rather than adding compute. It can fail when the workload's vision-token statistics differ from those used for calibration, when the low-attention vision-token assumption breaks on a new domain, or when text-heavy tasks suffer because text importance was only a preservation signal rather than the optimization target.
rationale: The method is training-free, runs on a single GPU, directly targets the dominant memory term in MoE-MLLMs, and provides code, making it immediately actionable under the stated constraints.
technique: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE MLLMs

claims.statement: MAEP replaces modality-agnostic expert-pruning importance metrics with a training-free, single-forward-pass metric that separates vision-side pruning signals from text-side preservation signals for MoE-based MLLMs. Cost is limited to a calibration forward pass and permanent removal of experts, with no retraining; inference speed is largely unchanged since it removes parameters rather than adding compute. It can fail when the workload's vision-token statistics differ from those used for calibration, when the low-attention vision-token assumption breaks on a new domain, or when text-heavy tasks suffer because text importance was only a preservation signal rather than the optimization target.
Reduces BF16 expert weights by ~27 GB (~47% of total memory), bringing a ~58 GB model into a single 40 GB GPU.
